toolset: Full Visual Studio MSBuild. Counts depend on this: the bare AllRules.ruleset only resolves on a Visual Studio host, so these numbers are NOT comparable with dotnet build or Linux logs. See README.md.
note: Maximum allowed occurrences per warning code. Regenerate with warnings.ps1 -UpdateBaseline after an intentional change and record why in notes.<CODE> and the commit message.

notes.CA1416: Floor is the budget of Windows coupling, not a count of visible diagnostics, and it is deliberately left at 488 although only 468 are currently visible. Extracting SplashScreen.cs into MediaPortal.Utilities.Windows removed 20 diagnostics without removing one Windows dependency: that assembly declares [SupportedOSPlatform("windows")], which makes CA1416 treat its OWN call sites as platform-neutral. The declaration is still worth it - it is what turns a call from portable code into a call-site diagnostic - but the consequence is that satellites are invisible to CA1416 from the inside. Downside stated plainly: up to 20 new Windows calls could be added before this floor complains. spine.ps1 is what closes that hole; it gates the *.Windows assemblies in their own section so quarantined code cannot grow. Lower 488 only when a Windows dependency is genuinely removed.
